title: Company Horizon Scenario Lab and OKRs (facilitation kit)
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a working facilitation kit for the leadership scenario-lab + company-wide OKR alignment session we want to run ahead of the March all-team meeting. Goal is to arrive at a small set of prioritized company objectives (3) with measurable KRs and a first-pass roll-out plan for Q2–Q3.

Context / quick background (notes to self):
- Executive ask: reduce operational complexity while increasing reliability and lowering unit cost for hosted inference.
- Recent signals: Dedicated sales uptick with three mid-market pilots; two customers requested VPC onboarding timelines.
- Tech constraints: serving-runtime team landed attention-kernel patch but we still need broader rollout + perf validation.
- This doc will be messy — use as sandbox for facilitation script + OKR drafts.

High-level agenda (90 minutes, remote/hybrid):
- 0–10m: Scene-setting (CEO — 2 slides), business context and top risks.
- 10–30m: Scenario lab intro + small-group breakout instructions (facilitator: Priya).
- 30–55m: Breakouts (3 rooms, 3 scenarios each) — 20m discussion + 5m capture.
- 55–75m: Report-outs (3 groups, 6m each) + immediate clarifying Qs.
- 75–85m: Exec reaction (benchmarks + constraints).
- 85–90m: Decisions and next steps (assign owners).

Facilitation checklist / logistics:
- Rooms: Zoom main + 3 breakout rooms. Prep doc and slide deck linked above.
- Materials to share in breakouts: scenario one-pager (attached), OKR canvas (Google slide), risk/assumption cards.
- Prep for leads: provide 2-minute summary, top-3 asks, and one data point.
- Capture: use shared Google sheet (tab per group) — link in Slack pinned message.
- Fallback plan: if breakout tech fails, pivot to unstructured chat and write notes in doc.

Scenario prompts (short):
1) Peak demand surge (x3 QPS) — limited burst capacity. How to prioritize traffic, degrade gracefully, and preserve latencies?
2) Regulated enterprise onboarding — private deployment + audit readiness under 60 days. What must we prioritize operationally?
3) 30% model cost reduction target — what tradeoffs (quantization, batching, model routing) are acceptable while maintaining quality?

Draft company-level OKRs (take these as starting points, quantifiable where possible):
Objective A: Make Redwood the predictable low-latency inference platform for product teams
- KR A1: Median P95 latency for text-generation across hosted models <= 160ms for origin traffic (baseline Feb 2025 = 210ms)
- KR A2: <1% incidents causing >2x latency spikes per quarter (SRE tracked)
- KR A3: Ship 2 runtime optimizations (kernel selection + KV cache eviction) with verified perf gains in our benchmark suite

Objective B: Drive down unit cost while protecting output quality for mid-market customers
- KR B1: Reduce per-token GPU cost for typical 8k seq workloads by 25% vs Jan 2025 baseline
- KR B2: Deploy model-routing policy that reduces expensive model usage by 18% without degrading eval prompt-set accuracy by >1.5%
- KR B3: Convert two pilot accounts to Dedicated reservations with minimum 6-month commit

Objective C: Operationalize Private deployments and compliance for regulated customers
- KR C1: Publish Private deployment onboarding blueprint and SSO/KMS playbook (DR and runbook included)
- KR C2: Achieve SOC2 readiness checklist completion for 80% of items in Q2 readiness audit
- KR C3: Reduce average Private onboarding time from inquiry to hand-off from 75 days to 45 days

Notes on measurement and ownership (rough):
- Ownership: A -> Serving-runtime + Platform eng; B -> Optimize + Product-hosted-api + Solutions eng; C -> Private-deployments + Security & compliance + Solutions eng
- Measurement owners: Eng reliability dashboards + Finance unit cost model + Product data team (for quality evals)
- Baselines: We need to finalize Jan 2025 baselines for latency and cost before committing to KRs. Action: Marcus to pull baseline dashboards (due 2025-02-14).

Exec update talking points (for CEO/CTO 5-min brief):
- Quick wins to call out: kernel opt merged, two Dedicated pilots entered POC, new routing prototype reduced cost 12% in internal A/B test.
- Open gaps: private onboarding runway, SOC2 item backlog, evaluation harness for routing impact.
- Asks for execs: clear decision on prioritization between Private onboarding vs. runtime cost optimizations if resource contention appears.

Risks and mitigations (light):
- Risk: Shipping perf changes without broad eval leads to customer regressions. Mitigation: gated rollout, canary on Dedicated pools and synthetic eval prompt sets.
- Risk: Over-index on cost at expense of quality. Mitigation: maintain fail-open policy and quality guardrails in code/config.
- Risk: Sales expectations misaligned with engineering timelines. Mitigation: Solutions eng to present realistic SLAs and ramp plan to sales by Feb 21.

Open questions / decisions needed (short list):
- Which single objective should get majority of engineering headcount for Q2? (A/B/C?)
- Acceptable regression window for routing experiments (KR B2): is 1.5% accuracy acceptable or too high?
- Firm commitment needed from Finance for Dedicated discounting thresholds before we commit to conversion KRs.

Quick action tracker (next two weeks):
- Marcus Li: pull latency and per-token cost baselines (due 2025-02-14).
- Elena Rodriguez: draft Private onboarding blueprint skeleton (due 2025-02-17).
- Samir Patel: prepare breakout one-pagers and OKR canvases (due 2025-02-12).
- Priya Kapoor: schedule facilitation dry run with execs (target 2025-02-19).

Post-session artifacts to produce:
- Consolidated OKR draft for exec review (v0.1)
- Risk register + decision log (Google sheet)
- Implementation roadmap (quarterly phases) with named owners

Notes to self / facilitation heuristics (half-baked):
- Keep scenarios tangible: use customer stories, not generic language.
- Force a decision at the end of the session — even if provisional.
- Use dot-vote to prioritize if we have >6 candidate KRs.
- Capture dissenting opinions in the decision log — important for post-mortem if things go sideways.

References / pointers:
- Confluence: company/horizon-2025-scene-setting (draft)
- JIRA: CORP-2150 (scenario lab logistics)
- Slack: #company-strategy (pins include breakout templates)

End of working draft.

---
Version notes: v0.1 initial facilitation kit; v0.2 will incorporate baseline numbers and exec feedback after dry run.
